hints: Focus on what happens as you go down Group 2, the atoms get bigger and reactivity generally increases.
Remember that Group 2 hydroxides get more soluble down the group, while sulfates do the opposite.
Check each option for increase versus decrease, and pick the one trend that falls from magnesium to barium.
walkthrough:
**Recall reactivity down Group 2**

Going from magnesium to barium, the atoms get larger and lose their two outer electrons more easily. So reactivity increases down the group.

Reaction example:
$$\text{M(s) + 2HCl(aq) \rightarrow MCl}_2\text{(aq) + H}_2\text{(g)}$$

**Check reaction rate and carbonate stability**

Because reactivity increases, the rate with dilute $\text{HCl}$ increases from Mg to Ba. Similarly, the carbonates become more thermally stable, so the decomposition temperature increases.

Decomposition example:
$$\text{MCO}_3\text{(s) \rightarrow MO(s) + CO}_2\text{(g)}$$

**Compare the two solubility trends**

This is the classic pair to learn together. Hydroxide solubility increases down the group, $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ is sparingly soluble but $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ is much more soluble. Sulfate solubility decreases down the group, $\text{MgSO}_4$ is soluble but $\text{BaSO}_4$ is insoluble.

**Pick the decreasing property**

Only one of the four properties falls from magnesium to barium. That is the solubility of the sulfates.

options.A: Incorrect. Reactivity increases down Group 2 as ionisation energy falls, so magnesium reacts steadily but barium reacts very vigorously with dilute HCl. The rate increases, not decreases.
options.B: Incorrect. The solubility of Group 2 hydroxides increases from magnesium to barium. Mg(OH)2 is almost insoluble while Ba(OH)2 gives a distinctly alkaline solution.
options.C: Correct. The solubility of Group 2 sulfates decreases down the group. MgSO4 is very soluble, CaSO4 is sparingly soluble, and BaSO4 is insoluble, which is why BaSO4 is used as a barium meal.
options.D: Incorrect. Carbonates become more stable to heat down the group because the larger cation polarises the carbonate ion less. So the temperature needed for decomposition increases from Mg to Ba.
